label: diffuse original-phase unit, boosted by digits/q/g/l context (no clean explanation)
explanation: Active on 5% of steps across 36% of sequences, with no clean trigger. About 79% of activation mass falls in the original phase. It never fires at t=0 and rarely at the delimiter. It is most often active at t=1-2 and at late original positions in long sequences (orig_idx 7-8, rate 16-23%). Firing is more likely on input tokens 2, l, 0, 1, z, c and when the sequence contains digits or q/g/x/y/l (the rate rises with n_digits, from 2.4% at 0 digits to 21% at 5). It often fires in contiguous runs within a sequence. Copy-phase activity is weaker and also diffuse, with occasional strong runs at the end of the copy phase. The best simple predicate (current input is a digit/l/z/c in the original phase, after an earlier digit/q/g/x/y/l) reaches only dev F1 0.36 (precision 0.32, mass recall 0.52). Adding a disjunction for early or late positions did not help. Magnitude claims beyond these rate tables were not checked.
